bounded_statement: The report's selected result labels a retained-subset conditional rate (27 events over the 36 boxes retained after screening, 0.7500 / 75.00%) as the 'Fledging success rate for the complete planned set of 48 deployed nest boxes', even though the declared scientific target and the governing task both require a rate over the complete planned set of 48 units; the correct complete-domain figure computable from the report's own accounting (27/48 = 56.25%) differs materially from the reported 75.00%.

counterevidence_considered.description: The same selected-result sentence discloses the true exposure denominator of 36 boxes, and the unit-accounting section transparently reports 48 planned, 36 retained, and 12 removed, so an attentive reader could reconstruct the mismatch. This mitigates concealment but does not cure the issue: the headline rate of 75.00% is still explicitly labeled as the rate 'for the complete planned set of 48 deployed nest boxes', which is false for that domain.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed as 36 within the mislabeled claim

evidence.description: The selected result states 0.7500 (75.00%) as the rate 'for the complete planned set of 48 deployed nest boxes' while its arithmetic is 27/36, the retained-subset conditional rate. Independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms 48 planned units, 5 removed for incomplete monitoring, 7 removed for no active clutch, 36 retained, and 27 retained boxes with at least one fledgling; the complete-domain rate would be 27/48 = 56.25%, not 75.00%.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the verdict three ways. First, I checked whether the phrase 'for the complete planned set of 48 deployed nest boxes' could be read as merely identifying the study rather than the rate's domain; the sentence grammar attaches the domain directly to 'Fledging success rate', and the declared scientific target section removes any ambiguity that the claim's domain is the 48-box planned set. Second, I checked whether the in-sentence disclosure of the 36-box denominator makes the report internally correct; disclosure of the arithmetic does not change that the stated domain (48 planned boxes) and the computed domain (36 retained boxes) disagree, and 75.00% is not a rate over 48 units under any reading. Third, I recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv (48 planned; NB-04, NB-11, NB-22, NB-30, NB-41 incomplete; NB-07, NB-15, NB-19, NB-26, NB-33, NB-38, NB-45 no clutch; 27 of 36 retained with >=1 fledgling) to rule out a data-entry explanation; the accounting is accurate, isolating the defect to the denominator-versus-label mismatch. The verdict survives.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py sets the exposure denominator to the retained count (`denominator = retained_n`, yielding 27/36) but interpolates that value into a sentence template that scopes the rate to the complete planned set of `planned` (48) boxes, so a subset-conditional statistic is presented under a complete-domain label.
